review.reason: Candidate 5 is publishable as supplied. Hole 1 is a reachable 494-yard par 5 with a substantial lake on the right side of play and fairway bunkers along the route. A safer line away from the shoreline preserves a staged route, while advancing more aggressively offers a chance to reach in two. Hole 2 is a dry 440-yard dogleg-left par 4: following the bend is the sensible route, while the tree-lined inside line and fairway bunker make cutting the corner a real choice rather than a free shortcut. Hole 3 is a dry, straight 198-yard par 3 with approach bunkers and substantial greenside sand on both sides; its target rewards distance control without imposing a water carry. The par-5/4/3 sequence, changing routing shapes, and single substantial lake give the round strong internal contrast. Recent rounds often feature water and doglegs, and reachable par 5s recur, but this combination of a wet opener, dry dogleg middle hole, and dry straight finisher is sufficiently distinct. Simulated shots-to-green of 2/2/1 and safe tee-option counts of 51/38/55 support a challenging but playable set; the previews show usable landing areas. No geometry change is needed.
